page: Amazon Web Services t1.micro is an entry-level burstable instance deployed on the Xen hypervisor. It operates on an i386 architecture, featuring 1 virtual CPU mapped to 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is allocated 0.6 GB of RAM, backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a 25 MB shared L3 cache. It contains no attached local storage, possesses no GPUs, and operates with a 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth specification.

Benchmark results highlight the shared and limited compute capacity of this generation. In single-core testing via stress-ng, the instance achieved a score of 1856.98, falling into the middle 50% band. However, multi-core stress-ng performance remains identical at 1856.98 due to the single-core allocation, positioning it in the bottom 10%. PassMark measurements also place it in the lower 10% across key metrics, with a CPU score of 1121.29 and extended instructions at 584.4. Memory bandwidth on small cached blocks registered 105.19 GB/sec, while static web serving reached 1.62 GB/sec and Redis SET performance delivered 0.37 million operations per second.

The hardware configuration provides a minimal resource baseline suitable for low-priority execution where continuous high utilization is not demanded. Because compute capacity is burstable and memory is tightly constrained to 0.6 GB without integrated local storage or dedicated hardware cryptographic offloads, throughput-sensitive operations face strict performance boundaries. The instance fits basic utility workloads such as lightweight administrative scripts, simple test environments, and low-traffic proof-of-concept deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services t1.micro is a legacy burstable instance based on the Xen hypervisor and i386 architecture. Powered by a single vCPU from an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the configuration includes 0.6 GB of memory, no local storage, and 0 Gbps baseline network throughput. In synthetic benchmarks, it delivers average single-core stress-ng performance at 1856.98 points, while multi-core metrics, PassMark CPU testing (1121.29), and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into the lower tier due to its single-thread constraint and minimal memory allocation. Redis SET throughput is limited to 0.37 million operations per second, with static web serving reaching 1.62 GB/sec. Without support for advanced vector instructions or local disks, the t1.micro represents an entry-level resource profile best suited for lightweight scripting, background management tasks, and low-traffic development or demonstration workloads.
